Holly Humberstone says she was having an identity crisis on a weekly basis
You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.
In her spare time, the singer-songwriter is literally a cat burglar.
"We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.
"He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us."
Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.
"OK, we've been coercing him into the house with treats," she admits. "He's just so cute.
"But we're not trying to keep him. We literally push him out every night."
Humberstone's excuse for this feline felony is that, last year, her parents sold her childhood home in Lincolnshire , external and moved to Wales – taking her pets with them.
One, a cat called Tsuki, had even been immortalised in the song Lucy as a confidante who listens to her problems but "never judges".
"Oh, she knows some secrets!" laughs the singer. "I'm so glad she can't talk."
"We actually tried to bring her to London with us, but she's a countryside cat and she hated it so much. We had to send her to Wales where she can be free and frolic."
Her parents' relocation was disruptive for the human Humberstones, too.
Their house, a "freezing cold, falling down" property 20 minutes outside of Grantham, played a huge part in the singer's success.
Her early EPs were all written there, inspiring the "wonky sonics" of her indie-leaning pop sound. The 2021 single Haunted House is even dedicated to the "friendly" spirits who inhabited the property.
"It's a place I always felt I could go back to, to remind myself of who I am," she says.
Instead, she spent 2025 "packing up 23 years of stuff my family and I had accumulated", from her old ballet shoes and poetry books to forgotten bits of jewellery.
The singer shared photos of her old bedroom, and the artefacts she'd rediscovered, while clearing out her parents' "haunted house" in Grantham (pictured, left).
The process was unsettling. Already grappling with the idea of leaving childhood behind, Humberstone found herself literally throwing away her past.
"I felt uprooted. I was having some sort of identity crisis almost weekly," she says.
So she did what she's always done, and poured those feelings into her second album, Cruel World, which entered the UK charts at number four earlier this year.
"Writing these songs felt like building myself a little shield and a kind of safety bubble," she says. "There's an escapist, fantasy element to so much of the album."
Maybe that's true, but Humberstone has always had the ability to locate a song's emotional core, and the lyrics on Cruel World don't disappoint.
" To lose somebody is to know you're only human, honey, " she sings on To Love Somebody , external , soothing her elder sister as she endures an agonising break-up.
Undeterred by that heartbreak, she throws herself headfirst into a new affair on Die Happy , external , declaring: " Hit the gas, I want it fast, want it reckless ."
But the most revealing song is the closing track, Beauty Pageant , external .
Fragile and raw, it's the sound of Humberstone in her dressing room, addressing the woman in the mirror who'd "die for the applause" but who struggles with the impossible beauty standards imposed on female artists.
Humberstone's biggest songs include Falling Asleep At The Wheel, The Walls Are Way Too Thin, Die Happy and Scarlett
"That's a song that I wasn't really setting out to write," she confesses.
"Writing about other people often feels easier than turning the magnifying glass on yourself."
The lyrics, she says, draw on a "very specific" mindset she acquired at her all-girls school in Grantham.
"It was drilled into me: You're all in competition. You're only rewarded if you're the best. And if you're not, you're worthless."
The experience "really warped the way I view other girls", she says.
Musical success made it worse. After winning the Brits Rising Star award in 2022 , Humberstone found herself competing with megastars, even though her music leaned towards the alternative side of pop.
"I'm a very small fish and I recognise that, but suddenly I was in meetings being compared to all these people on my label's roster, who are on a completely different scale," she says.
"It's something I really, really struggled with in the early days and it's something I've really had to unlearn."
Nowadays, Humberstone has stopped benchmarking herself against her peers, recognising that the need for validation never fades.
"I don't think that there's a point I could get to, or an award that I could win, where these feelings would disappear," she says.
"Everybody feels like they've still got something to prove, so I'm done with setting myself goals - because then I lose sight of the real reason that I'm doing this, which is to write music that represents me, and have other people feel understood through that music."
"I pray that one day I'll turn and face the mirror with a smile," sings Humberstone
That mindset comes to fruition in the new, expanded edition of Cruel World, whose five new songs were largely written after the original album was handed in.
"I was super proud of Cruel World and, when you've got that in your back pocket, there's room to experiment and break some of your usual parameters."
The new tracks find Humberstone embracing a new persona – more confident, more flirtatious, a little salty – with music inspired by a playlist featuring Abba, Madonna and Robyn.
The single Too Cute To Be Lonely , external is a will-they/won't-they story set at a house party.
" Don't leave a girl upset, in such a pretty dress ," she teases the object of her affections.
Terminally Yours takes place a couple of weeks later, when Humberstone realises she's fallen head-over-heels in love.
" Your stupid face is my sorry fate ," she harrumphs, cross at herself. " For [expletive]'s sake, I'm in love ."
Silver Sky, a gorgeous acoustic ballad, tells another side of the story, as she settles into her lover's arms and drifts into blissful reverie.
"I wrote that on a kind of Hail Mary trip, seeing what fell out of the air in Nashville," she reveals.
"We went over to [co-writer Maddie Diaz's] house, took a guitar into the garden and wrote Silver Sky outside, while all of these gorgeous red cardinals were singing around us.
"I usually write a lot about my mental health struggles, but I was just in the mood to write something that made me feel good."
Humberstone won the Brits Rising Star award in 2022, joining the ranks of former winners such as Sam Fender, Florence + The Machine and Adele
Not that her mental health issues are in the rear view mirror. Humberstone admits her stage nerves have only intensified since the release of Cruel World.
"It's the proudest I've been of any of my work and, for that reason, I struggled with shows because I felt a lot of pressure to go out and deliver it to the standard that I think people are expecting.
"But on the other hand, it's totally fine if you mess up or sing a wrong note. People can't connect to a pop star that feels too robotic and polished.
"So maybe my strength is that vulnerability, and I need to recognise that more."
That vulnerability has won Humberstone millions of fans, even if a hit single has (so far) eluded her.
And her audience keeps growing. In May this year, her breakout single Falling Asleep At The Wheel was awarded a silver disc... five years after its release, indicating that her songs have staying power in an era of disposable hits.
Astonishingly, this is news to Humberstone, who learns about the accolade during our interview. But it helps to clarify a thought that's been knocking around her head.
"If I'm going to be doing this for years to come, I've just got to keep making music that feels right, trusting my gut and realising there's no en…

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw80:
Noel Fielding has said he is "appalled" by jokes he made alongside Russell Brand when the pair appeared together on TV and at live shows.
The Great British Bake Off presenter said in a statement to the Sun he was "horrified and deeply disturbed" to learn of Brand's crimes, after the disgraced comedian was jailed for rape and sexual assault.
Footage of Fielding and Brand joking about rape with TV presenter Jonathan Ross on an episode of Channel 4's Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2007 has resurfaced in the aftermath of Brand's conviction.
Fielding described "some of the jokes" he made as "horrible and inappropriate", and said he had not been in contact with Brand "for many years".
"I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand's crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice," Fielding said.
"I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years.
"Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them."
Ross has also released a statement distancing himself from the remarks, saying that his "thoughts are with the many, many women who have bravely come forward."
Among the resurfaced footage is a clip of Brand and Fielding laughing on an episode of The Russell Brand Show, which aired on BBC Radio 2 in 2007. In it, Brand joked about kissing and holding an underage grasshopper.
"How do you even know if it's a child or an adult? You don't even care, do you," Fielding responded.
Brand can be heard replying: "It's a mistake I've made. I've had a lot of problems in the past, because I thought a grasshopper was above age. Before I know it, I'm in it, right, I'm kissing it, I'm holding it. Then it turns around and looks at me with onyx eyes and says: 'I'm 12.'"
Brand and Fielding also performed charity gigs together as The Goth Detectives.
Fielding said he was "appalled" by some of the jokes he had made alongside Brand
Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others.
Further allegations against him have been made in recent days. More women have made allegations about him in interviews with the Times and a Netflix documentary.
The Times said it could not publish the investigation until the criminal case ended. Brand has denied non-consensual sexual activity.
Police have said Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women.
The disgraced entertainer is being detained at HMP Wandsworth. BBC News has asked his legal representatives for a response to the latest allegations.
If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

A Milli Kadın Basketbol Takımı, 2027 FIBA Avrupa Şampiyonası Elemeleri 2. tur I Grubu ikinci maçında İsrail'i 76-67 yendi.
Karşılaşmaya iyi başlayan ay-yıldızlılar, üst üste bulduğu 7 sayıyla 4. dakikaya 10-4 önde girdi. Üç sayı çizgisinin gerisini etkili kullanan Türkiye, ilk periyodu 22-10 üstün tamamladı.
Milliler, ikinci çeyrekte yakaladığı 8 sayılık seriyle rakibine kolay hücum etme şansı vermedi ve 13. dakikada İsrail'e mola aldırdı. Pota altını iyi kullanan ay-yıldızlı ekip, 15. dakikada Elif Bayram'ın basketiyle rakibiyle arasındaki farkı 13 sayıya çıkardı: 22-35. İsrail'in savunmadaki kötü oyununu Alperi Onar ve Meltem Yıldızhan ile iyi değerlendiren milli takım, soyunma odasına 47-29 önde gitti.
İkinci yarıya rahat başlayan Türkiye, 26. dakikada İsrail ile arasındaki farkı 20'ye yükseltti: 40-60. Çekişmeli geçen son bölümde İsrail 9 sayılık seri yakalasa da üçüncü periyot, millilerin 60-49 üstünlüğüyle sonuçlandı.
Son çeyrekte İsrail, boyalı alanı iyi kullanan taraf oldu ve 36. dakikada farkı tek sayıya indirdi: 55-64. Müsabakanın son saniyeleri büyük heyecana sahne oldu. İsrail, arka arkaya bulduğu 3 sayılık atışlarla farkı kapatmaya çalışırken Gökşen Fitik, başarılı serbest atışlarıyla farkın erimesine izin vermedi. Ay-yıldızlılar, karşılaşmadan 76-67 galip ayrıldı.
Türkiye'nin Letonya Büyükelçisi Ahmet Cemil Miroğlu ile Türkiye Basketbol Federasyonu Yönetim Kurulu üyeleri, mücadeleyi salonda takip etti.
Milliler, gruptaki 3. maçında 17 Kasım Salı günü TSİ 19.00'da Polonya'ya konuk olacak.
A Milli Kadın Basketbol Takımı'nda başantrenör Frederic Dusart ile milli basketbolcu Alperi Onar, Rimi Olympic Centre'da oynanan karşılaşmanın ardından AA muhabirine açıklamalarda bulundu.
İlk yarıda iyi bir oyun sergilediklerini kaydeden Fransız başantrenör, "İsrail'in vazgeçmeyen bir takım olduğunu ve savunmalarının bir problem olacağını biliyorduk. İlk yarı iyi iş çıkardık. İkinci yarıda ne oldu bilmiyorum. Sanırım biraz rahatladık ve geriye çekildik. Mental olarak oyunun dışına çıkmaya başladık. Kazanmak güzel ama özellikle ikinci yarıdaki oyunumuzla kazanmak benim için iyi bir şey değil. Polonya karşısında ikinci yarıdaki oyunumuz gibi oynamak yeterli olmayacaktır." diye konuştu.
Dusart, 17 Kasım Salı günü oynayacakları Polonya maçının zor olacağını belirterek, "Takımda Avrupa Ligi tecrübesi olan kaliteli oyuncular var. Polonya maçına odaklanmadan önce nasıl en iyi şekilde oynayabileceğimizin üzerine çalışmalıyız. Bugün 35 dakika boyunca iyi oynadık ancak bu Polonya karşısında yeterli olmayacaktır. Öncelikle hatalarımızı düzeltmeliyiz. Sonrasında Polonya maçı hakkında konuşabiliriz." ifadelerini kullandı.
Milli oyuncu Alperi Onar, eleme maçlarında her mücadeleyi kazanmanın önemli olduğunu vurguladı.
Frederic Dusart'ın yeni sistemine alışma aşamasında olduklarını anlatan Alperi, şunları söyledi:
"Kazanmak önemliydi. Yeni hocamızın yeni sistemine alışıyoruz ve ilk kamptan arka arkaya maçlar oynuyoruz. Fazla antrenman yapma fırsatımız olmuyor. Enerjimizle ilk yarıda orayı dengeledik ancak ikinci yarıda iniş ve çıkışlarımız oldu. Pencere maçlarında en önemli şey kazanmak. Eminim ki gelişerek ve büyüyerek devam edeceğiz."
Alperi, Polonya karşılaşmasında daha sert savunma yapmaları gerektiğini dile getirerek, "Hücumsal olarak yeni hocamıza alışmaya çalışıyoruz. Ama savunmada enerjimizi vermeliyiz ve daha istekli olmalıyız. Polonya iyi bir takım. Bu iki maçı ders olarak alacağız, bu maçları kazanmak önemliydi. Hatalarımızı düzeltmeye çalışacağız. Yarın Polonya'ya gideceğiz. Hazırlanmak için bir günümüz var. O yüzden olabildiğince hazır olup kazanmak için mücadelemizi vereceğiz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.

Oyuncu Deniz Türkali ile İtalyan şarkıcı Ernesto Casalini'nin kızı olan şarkıcı Zeynep Casalini , 2010 yılında restoran işletmecisi Tahsin Berk'le Bodrum'da evlenmişti.
Evlendikten sonra yaptığı açıklamada eşi için “Şu an çok güzel bir evlilik yaşıyorum. Dünyanın en yakışıklı adamıyla evli olduğumu düşünüyorum. Eşimin tek bir şeyi değil, her şeyi beni etkiledi. Hayatı algılayışı, duruşu, fikirleri, her şeyi bana büyüleyici geldi" diyen Casalini, bir sene sonra da kızı Dafne'yi dünyaya getirdi.
Ancak Zeynep Casalini ile Tahsin Berk, 2016 yılında boşandı. Boşandıktan bir sene sonra yeniden bir araya gelen ve Bodrum'da ortak olan çift, yeniden evlendi.
Zeynep Casalini ile Tahsin Berk, boşandıktan tam 10 yıl sonra yeniden nikah masasına oturdu. Nikahta üzerinde yıldızlar bulunan siyah bir mini elbise giyen Casalini, kombinini tül duvakla tamamladı.
Nikah masasında çekilen fotoğraflarını ve kızları Dafne'yle verdikleri pozu takipçileriyle paylaşan Casalini, “Anlatılmaz yaşanır” notunu düştü.
Uzun yıllar önce vegan olduğunu açıklayan 56 yaşındaki Zeynep Casalini'nin paylaşımına birçok tebrik yorumu geldi.
Şarkıcı Hande Yener de meslektaşına “Tebrikler Zeynepçiğim. mutluluklar diliyorum” diye seslendi.
Zeynep Casalini'nin müzik hayatı lise yıllarında başladı. İtalya ve İngiltere'deki çalışmaları sonrası Türkiye'ye dönen Casalini Sezen Aksu, Emel Müftüoğlu gibi birçok ismin vokalliğini yaptı. 2004 yılında kendi albümünü çıkaran şarkıcı, “Duvar”, “Köprüler”, “Ne Yapsam” ve “Dokunma Bana” şarkılarıyla tanındı. Gözlerden uzak bir yaşam süren Casalini, müzik çalışmalarını sürdürüyor.

Samandıra'da bulunan Fenerbahçe Can Bartu Tesisleri'nde sarı-lacivertli ekibin antrenmanından önce basın mensuplarıyla bir araya gelen teknik direktör Belözoğlu, takımdaki değişimden hedeflerine dek birçok soruyu yanıtladı.
Fenerbahçe'de oynatmak istediği oyunla ilgili Belözoğlu, "Kendi kendine oyuncudan oyuna gidecek bir yapı inşa etmemiz gerekiyor. Kazanma odaklı, net planları olan, savunma planlarını artıracağımız bir oyun hedefliyoruz. Bu takım savunma konusunda, dünyanın en güçlü ekiplerinden Liverpool'a bunu yapacağını gösterdi. Dünyanın en küçük takımları bile sert blok antrenmanları yapıyor. Bugün test yaptık, herkes iyi durumda. Fenerbahçe fizik olarak herkesi karşılayabilir. Her şeyin içinde bir planın olduğu oyun uygulamayı hedefliyoruz. Bunun için de çalışıyoruz. İnşallah bu fotoğrafı en kısa sürede herkese izleteceğiz." şeklinde konuştu.
Samandıra'da teknik kadrodan sağlık ekibine dek yaşanan değişimle ilgili soruyu "Olması gerekiyordu." diyerek yanıtlayan Belözoğlu, "Yaşanan değişimin ötesinde bir şey yok. Ben bir ekiple geldim. Samandıra'da değişim gerekiyordu. Gelenler mükemmel, gidenler kötüymüş gibi bir durum yok. Bunu doğru bulmuyorum. Emeği geçen çok kişi var. Tamamen değişimle ilgili bir durum söz konusu. Belirlediğimiz noktalar vardı ve hızlı hareket etmek durumundaydık. Bu bir bayrak yarışı, bunu biz devraldık. Elimizden gelenin fazlasını yapmaya çalışacağız. Değişimin ötesinde başka bir durum yok. Emeği geçenlere teşekkür ediyorum. İnsanların aileleri var, burada değerlendirme yaparken buna dikkat etmek gerekiyor. Gidenler de değerli isimlerdi." ifadelerini kullandı.
Fenerbahçe'de farklı bir futbol oynatmaları gerektiğinin altını çizen Emre Belözoğlu, dünyada atlet futbolcuların önemli hale geldiğini belirtti.
Sarı-lacivertli takımın oynadığı futbol anlamında bir geçmişe sahip olduğunu vurgulayan Belözoğlu, "Fenerbahçe'de oyunun genetiği var. Büyük bir camia beklentisi var. Fenerbahçe'nin oyunu için de gerekenleri söylemiştim, kalite ve tutku. Bazı maçlarda işin içine akıl girecek. Bazı maçlarda farklı kelimeler olacak. Bunun olmazsa olmazı kalite. Ne kadar hızlanacağımızı göreceğiz. Ümidim bunu hızlı yapmak. Başlangıcımız fena olmadı. Ama tek çiçekle bahar gelmiyor, bunun suni olmamasını arzu ediyorum." açıklamasını yaptı.
Şu anda gündemlerinin ilk oynanacak Kocaelispor maçı olduğunun altını çizen Belözoğlu, "Gündemimiz ocakta yapacağımız hamleler ve takımın eksikleri değil. Fenerbahçe'nin net bir gücü var. İdmanda hissediyorum, oyuncuyla konuşunca hissediyorum, ilk oynadığımız maçta hissettim. Bugün gündemimiz hamle ve Trabzonspor maçı değil. Gündemimiz tamamen Kocaelispor maçı, sonra Shakhtar maçı olacak. Ciddi şekilde takıma merhem olacak organizasyonu inşa etmemiz gerekiyor. Zamanı geldiğinde değerlendirmeler yapmamız gerekiyor. Milli takım arası oldu, bu bir avantaj. Bazı oyuncular milli takımlara çağrılmadı, onlara ufak dokunuşlarımız olacak. Fenerbahçe'de başarı kriteri performanstır. Kocaelispor maçına kadar takımı ne kadar hazırlayabilirim, bunun derdindeyim." diye konuştu.
Emre Belözoğlu, Fenerbahçe'de en büyük arzusunun, altyapıdan yetişen oyunculara şans vermek olduğunu dile getirdi.
Daha önce sarı-lacivertli kulüpte önce sportif direktörlük ardından da teknik adamlık yaptığını hatırlatan Belözoğlu, "O dönemde oynattığımız genç isimler oldu. Bu, büyük bir hedef. Ama gerçekçi bakmak lazım, elimizdeki en iyi ve en güçlü kadroyla sahaya çıkmamız gerekiyor. Yiğit Efe Demir şu anda en değerli oyuncularımızdan biri. Hem lig hem de Avrupa tecrübesi var. Genç ve tecrübeli bir oyuncudan bahsediyoruz. Her futbolcuya ihtiyacımız var." dedi.

Kimi için bol limonlu bir midye dolma, kimi için gece yarısı yenilen sıcacık bir kokoreç, kimi için de bol malzemeli bir dürüm vazgeçilmezdir.
Peki ya hayatın boyunca yalnızca tek bir sokak lezzeti yiyebilecek olsaydın?
Senin için yemek yemek yalnızca karnını doyurmak değil, gerçek bir keyif meselesi. Herkesin tercih ettiği güvenli seçeneklere yönelmek yerine karakteri olan, iddialı ve kendine özgü lezzetleri seviyorsun. Kokoreç seçmen, güçlü tatlardan korkmadığını ve ne istediğini bildiğini gösteriyor. Bir sokak tezgâhının önünde durduğunda uzun uzun düşünmez, canın ne çekiyorsa onu söylersin. Üstelik yanında bol baharat, biraz acı ve soğuk bir içecek de varsa keyfin tamamdır. Senin hayat anlayışında küçük mutlulukların yeri büyük. Gece acıktığında, arkadaşlarınla dışarı çıktığında veya plansız bir sokak turuna başladığında kendini en mutlu hissettiğin anları yaşayabilirsin. Biraz spontane, biraz iştahlı ve kesinlikle sıradanlıktan uzak birisin. Kokoreç senin için yalnızca bir yemek değil; kendine has bir ritüel.
Senin için lezzetin en güzel hâli, her lokmada biraz daha devam eden bir keyif. Midye dolma seçmen, tek bir şeye bağlı kalmadan küçük küçük mutluluklar biriktirmeyi sevdiğini düşündürüyor. Bir tane yiyip bırakmak yerine tabağın başında zamanın nasıl geçtiğini unutabilirsin. Limonu bol, pirinci tam kıvamında ve baharatı yerinde olacak. Üstelik kaç tane yediğini saymayı da pek sevmiyorsun! Sosyal, meraklı ve anın tadını çıkarmayı bilen bir tarafın var. Arkadaşlarınla sahilde yürümek, bir şeyler atıştırmak, sohbet etmek ve plansızca uzayan akşamlar sana iyi geliyor olabilir. Senin için önemli olan yalnızca ne yediğin değil, o sırada kimlerle olduğun ve nasıl hissettiğin. Midye dolma seçimin, hayatı küçük ama tekrar tekrar yaşamak isteyeceğin anlarla güzelleştirdiğini söylüyor.
Senin için bazı lezzetlerin modası asla geçmez. Islak hamburger seçmen, gösterişten çok tanıdık ve güvenilir tatları sevdiğini anlatıyor. Bol soslu, yumuşacık ekmeği ve kendine özgü kokusuyla bu hamburger senin gözünde sıradan bir atıştırmalık değil. Belki de gece dışarı çıktıktan sonra yenilen o meşhur hamburgerin verdiği mutluluğu hiçbir restoran yemeği veremiyordur. Sen küçük ritüellerine bağlı, anılarla güçlü bağ kuran birisin. Bir şarkı, bir sokak, bir koku veya bir yemek seni yıllar öncesine götürebilir. Çok büyük beklentiler peşinde koşmak yerine bildiğin şeylerin tadını çıkarmayı tercih edersin. Hayatın her zaman kusursuz olmasına gerek yok; bazen iyi bir hamburger, sevdiğin insanlar ve güzel bir akşam bütün sorunları birkaç dakikalığına unutturabilir.

Doyurucu, lezzetli ve her zaman güvenebileceğin bir tercih ararsın. Döner dürüm tam da bu yüzden senin vazgeçilmezin. Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ile COP31 Türkiye iş birliğinde, “Dünya Ortak Evimiz” üst başlığıyla hayata geçirilen festival; küresel iklim krizine, çevresel felaketlere, kuraklığa ve ekolojik yıkımlara sinemanın gücüyle dikkat çekiyor.
Kurmaca, belgesel ve animasyon olmak üzere 3 kategoride dünyanın dört bir yanından yüzlerce eserin başvurduğu yarışmada jüri değerlendirmesinin ardından finale kalan 10 güçlü yapımı sinemaseverlerle buluşturuyor.
Dünyanın dört bir yanından gelen başvuruların değerlendirildiği yarışmanın ön jüri üyeliğini Mustafa Gürbüz, Ömer Dişbudak ve Merve Kuş Mataracı üstlendi.
Ön değerlendirmeyi geçen finalist filmler ise usta yönetmen Derviş Zaim'in başkanlığında; oyuncular Perihan Savaş ve Fikret Kuşkan, görüntü yönetmeni Feza Çaldıran ile yönetmen Darin J. Sallam'dan oluşan saygın bir ana jüri tarafından değerlendirildi.
Bu akşam saat 20.30'da COP31 Yeşil Alan'daki Kongre Salonu'nda gerçekleşecek yarışmada, dereceye giren sinemacılara çeşitli ödüller verecek. Dereceye giren finalistler sürdürülebilirlik vurgusu taşıyan, endüstriyel atıklar ve geri dönüştürülmüş malzemelerden özel olarak tasarlanan caretta caretta figürlü ödül heykelcikleri de verilecek.
COP31 Kısa Film Festivali kapsamında, Türk sinemasının usta sanatçıları da söyleşilere katılıyor. Ünlü sanatçı Hülya Koçyiğit, Berlin'de Altın Ayı kazanarak sinema tarihimizin ilk uluslararası başarısına imza atan başyapıtı Susuz Yaz ile COP31 İklim Temalı Kısa Film Yarışması'nın konuğu oluyor.
Koçyiğit, saat 17.30'da sinema yazarı Aslıhan Saraçoğlu moderatörlüğünde; su, doğa ve insan ilişkisini sanatçı perspektifiyle değerlendirecek.
Sanatçı ve yönetmen Uğur Yücel de saat 18.30'da senarist ve yapımcı Suat Köçer moderatörlüğünde; insan-doğa ilişkileri, değişen sinema seyirci algısı ve dijitalleşmenin etkileri üzerine gözlemlerini paylaşacak.
Filistinli yönetmen Darin J.Sallam da yönetmen Abdullah Harun İlhan moderatörlüğünde gerçekleşecek buluşmada, işgalin doğa ve canlılar üzerindeki ekolojik yıkımlarını ve Filistin direnişinin sinemadaki yansımalarını aktaracak.
COP31 Kısa Film Festivali kapsamında ayrıca mülkiyet, su hakkı ve kuraklık temalarını sinematik bir dille ele alan Metin Erksan imzalı Susuz Yaz filminin özel gösterimi yapılacak.
Film gösterimleri, Hülya Koçyiğit ve Uğur Yücel söyleşilerinin ardından saat 20.30'da ödül töreni düzenlenecek. Çok sayıda davetli ve sinemacıların katılacağı gecenin sunuculuğunu ise ünlü oyuncular Cem Davran ve Ekin Olcayto üstleniyor.

Ay Yapım bünyesindeki yapay zeka stüdyosu AI Yapım'ın hazırladığı Çukur Vartolu projesi bir festivalde gösterildi. Gösterimde Erkan Kolçak Köstendil'in dijital figürünün yer aldığı görüldü. Oyuncular Sendikası konuyla ilgili kamuoyuna resmi bir bildiri yayımladı. Köstendil de sosyal medyada tepkisini gösterdi.
Kriz, WAIFF isimli festivalde gösterimi yapılan yapay zeka destekli film projesinde ortaya çıktı. Ay Yapım bünyesinde faaliyet gösteren yapay zeka prodüksiyon stüdyosu AI Yapım'ın hazırladığı Çukur Vartolu projesinde, Çukur dizisinde Vartolu Sadettin'i canlandıran Erkan Kolçak Köstendil'in dijital figürü yer aldı. Köstendil'in bu dijital kopyanın oluşturulmasına rızasının bulunmadığı belirtildi.
Oyuncular Sendikası, WAIFF festivalinde gösterilen projede Köstendil'in dijital figürünün yer aldığını tespit ettiklerini ve oyuncunun bu figürün oluşturulmasına rızasının bulunmadığını sendikaya bildirdiğini duyurdu. Sendika, kamuoyuna ve meslektaşlarına yönelik yayımladığı bildiride şu ifadelere yer verdi:
'Her şeyden önce şu gerçeğin altını çizmek isteriz. Sadece bir oyuncunun değil, hiçbir insanın görüntüsü ve sesi kendi açık rızası olmadan dijital ortamda kopyalanamaz ve modellenemez. Hiçbir oyuncunun görüntüsü, sesi ve ayırt edici kişisel özellikleri, geçmişte gerçekleştirdiği bir performansa dayanılarak, iradesi dışında yeni dijital performanslar üretmek amacıyla sınırsız biçimde kullanılamaz. Bir kişinin iradesi dışında dijital kopyasının oluşturulması, hiç gerçekleştirmediği davranışların ve söylemediği sözlerin kendisine atfedilmesi ve bunların ticari amaçlarla kullanılması, kişilik hakları bakımından ciddi hukuki sorunlar doğurduğu gibi icracı haklarımız açısından da hukuka aykırılık teşkil etmektedir.'
Canlandırdığı karakterin dijital bir ikizinin kendisinden habersiz üretilmesine tepki gösteren Köstendil, projede kullanılan görseli kişisel Instagram hesabından paylaştı. Oyuncu paylaşımında şu ifadeleri kullandı:
' Yapay zeka teknolojisi gelişti ne güzel, aferin yaratıcı genç çocuklar sizi. Yalnız ben bunu bir aktöre benzettim, sizce kime benziyor? Yorumlarda buluşalım.'
Köstendil tepkisini sözlü açıklamayla sınırlı tutmadı. Oyuncu, yıllarca başrolünde yer aldığı Çukur dizisine ilişkin geçmiş yıllarda sosyal medya hesabında paylaştığı tüm görsel ve içerikleri profilinden sildi. Oyuncular Sendikası ise bildirisinde Köstendil'in yanında olduklarını ve haklarını korumak adına gerekli tüm adımları atacaklarını kamuoyuna duyurdu. Gelişme, sektörde yapay zeka ve oyuncu hakları konusunda yeni bir hukuki tartışmanın kapısını araladı.

The UN climate chief has warned that "tactical delays" at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey could prevent a deal to slow global warming.
The United Nations' top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey to "avoid tactical delays" that would prevent a deal to stop global warming.
Delegates from more than 200 nations are gathered in the Mediterranean city of Antalya with the core goal of preventing the planet from warming by 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit).
Downtown, thousands of civil society and environmental activists from around the world protested against the consequences of climate change .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), said getting an agreement is "tough but vital work."
"There ​is no collective success without compromise from every party," he added.
"As we head into the second week, ​I urge ‌parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and to avoid tactical delays."
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of protesters marched through Antalya on Saturday for climate protection and human rights, according to organizers.
Many were dismayed at the lack of progress and how the climate crisis is taking a back seat.
"The pursuit of profit at all costs continues to set the [global] agenda [and] govern the trajectory of our world, so there is a need to push back," environmental activist Zaki Mamdoo from South Africa told DW.
Luisa Nebauer, the main organizer of Germany's Fridays for Future movement, lamented that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was absent from the conference, along with several other European leaders.
"We won't have a chance to solve any of the crises as long as our planet is destabilizing by the hour," Nebauer told DW. "We must show up!"
Turkish authorities permitted the rally to go ahead, in a country that often bans large public gatherings.
Alongside the march, a parallel "People's Climate Summit" involving hundreds of domestic and international civil society groups takes place in Antalya this weekend.
With inflation, wars, deindustrialization and debt being seen as bigger immediate threats, many governments are watering down their commitments to the clean energy transition, along with the billions required to help developing nations to adapt.
The United ⁠States has snubbed the talks ​for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called climate change a hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.
Delegates also face pressure from large fossil-fuel-producing nations to avoid setting stricter targets for a faster phaseout of oil and gas.
Climate advocates in Antalya are growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of commitment and delaying tactics preventing an ambitious deal.
COP31 is seeking to unlock finance and investment , reduce the use of so-called super-pollutants and methane and ensure food security.
Host Turkey is, meanwhile, pushing a plan to expand global electrification. Yet, some environmental groups are disappointed the proposal doesn't push increased electricity use from renewable sources.
A UN report last month warned that, within a few years, the world is set to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming.
The figure, set at COP21 in 2015, is the threshold beyond which most scientists believe the world will see increasingly extreme effects of climate change.
A first draft of a deal text is expected to emerge next week, according to Australia's ​COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen.

Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night.
This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004 . And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].”
Asked to respond to those words, and whether Spain still had work to do combating racism after being fined for discriminatory chants about Muslims during a game against Egypt in Barcelona in March, the Spain coach asked for confirmation as to whom they had come from, then said: “I can say the opposite. Tell Thomas there is no racism. As clear as that. Exactly the same as in England. We’re not racists, none of us.”
Tuchel, speaking later on Saturday night, expressed his irritation with the media, accusing journalists of manufacturing a row. “I got asked ‘what will happen if and if and if’, and I said if it happens, we have a protocol in place. That’s it … I never talked about racism in Spain, I answered politely a question about what happens. You create a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing.”
De la Fuente also described Spain versus England as “one of the best games you can see anywhere in the world right now, maybe the best”, and admitted that his team needs to exercise more control than they had been able to do during their 3-2 win at Wembley in September.
Asked to explain how the Premier League could be the richest league in the world and English players command bigger transfer fees than Spaniards despite the national team not winning anything since 1966 while the selección have won two World Cups and three Euros in this century alone, he insisted that it is a mistake to mix price and value.
“There is a song about value and price and it is exactly that,” the Spain coach said. “Someone has to pay it and that’s very welcome but it doesn’t mean it is the real value. I am surprised often when you see the prices paid for our players compared to [the fees] paid in England. I think ‘they’re so cheap’. They [Spanish players] are the best in the world. You can buy a player for half the price of what you pay in England for someone. In that world, in that market, that’s what’s spent. But I’m clear on this: we must not confuse price and value.
“Between the English model and the Spanish model, I would choose the Spanish model,” De la Fuente added. “It is recognisable and the players have the ability to express it. The English model has developed a lot and I think it is very good. But you have to have the players. We can’t play like them and they can’t play like us.
“One of the strengths England have is the ability to run into space. When the game is open, they have people who are comfortable with that space and playing that style. Last time against them we lacked control, were unable to have longer periods of possession and impose ourselves more on our opponents.
“In the last two tournaments, England have been third and finalists. I think they are a great team and they have great players. That shows you it is not easy to win. Maybe that should make us appreciate what we’re doing this century: it is marvellous and very difficult. England are always candidates to win everything [nowadays]. This is one of the best games you can see in the world.”

Luis de la Fuente agreed a contract extension in September to stay as Spain boss until 2032
Luis de la Fuente has dismissed concerns over racism in Spanish football before the national team's Uefa Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday.
Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3.
While he has stressed he didn't expect there to be any incidents, the visit will be England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players.
Spain head coach De la Fuente was asked whether Tuchel's message to his players showed there was still work needed to tackle racism in Spain.
But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.
"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."
The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona.
In the domestic game, Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr has been a vocal anti-racism campaigner after frequently being on the end of racist chanting - and worse. In 2024 three Valencia fans were sentenced to eight months in prison for abusing him at a match.
Uefa operates a three-step protocol, allowing referees to stop matches, take players off the pitch temporarily and, ultimately, abandon a game if discriminatory behaviour continues.
Tuchel said on Friday: "Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."
However, when asked again about his views at a pre-match news conference on Saturday, Tuchel added: "I never talk about racism in Spain.
"I answered politely a question about what happens, I never expect racism. I got asked, 'what will happen if and if and if?'. And I said, 'if it happens, there's a protocol in place'. That's it.
"But my trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: brings people together and not divide people."
Midfielder Declan Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro and Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place that we followed - we came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
"The times we are in now, 2026, there should never be racism in football. It's shocking we still have it in the game today.
"I don't want to think about if one of our players or their players is racially abused because that would be a horrible mark on football."
Focusing on the match itself, De la Fuente believed both teams are currently at the pinnacle of world football, although he rejected the suggestion one could simply replicate the other's playing style.
Spain were crowned World Cup winners in the summer, while England finished third after losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.
"I prefer the Spanish model. It's very recognisable, the players are perfectly adapted," said De la Fuente. "The English model is very good, but you have to have that type of player. Neither England can play like Spain, nor Spain like England."
He suggested Spain had faced increasingly aggressive opposition as their recent success had raised expectations.
"It's our best moment in a long time," added De la Fuente, whose side also lifted the Euro 2024 title by beating England. "They are all much more aggressive to beat us now than in other times."
He also defended the value of Spanish players, arguing their performances often outweighed their transfer-market prices compared with those in the Premier League.
"Spanish footballers surprise me that, compared to what is paid in England, they are very cheap," he explained. "I see them as better, in my opinion. Everyone in their market can set the prices."
On the fitness of forward Lamine Yamal, he remained cautious over whether the Barcelona teenager would start or how long he could manage.
"We will see if he is a starter, but if he comes out, it's because he's fit to play," said De la Fuente.
Spain test will reveal if Tuchel and England have learned World Cup lessons

England play their final Nations League group game in Madrid against Spain on Sunday; Three Lions will win Group A3 with victory over world champions; follow Spain vs England in our live blog on the Sky Sports website and App on Sunday, kick-off 7.45pm
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.
Tuchel was asked after England's win over Croatia on Thursday how he and England would react if racist abuse occurred during Sunday's game against Spain.
The head coach responded by saying he would "maybe take five minutes" to remind his players of the anti-racism protocols. Tuchel also said "we will not expect" any abuse to occur in Madrid.
The game is England's first visit to the Spanish capital since 2004, when the match was marred by racist abuse directed at England's black players.
Spain were also fined and handed a partial stadium closure last month as punishment for Islamophobic chanting in Barcelona during a game against Egypt in March.
Luis de la Fuente was asked on Saturday by a Spanish-based English journalist: "Does the fact we keep talking about this topic demonstrate that Spanish football still has work to do in the fight against racism?"
In response, the Spain boss said: "What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it.
"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."
Tuchel was then asked by a Spanish journalist about his counterpart's comments, to which he responded: "I was polite enough to ask [sic - answer] a question from your colleagues.
"And you run and ask the other coach, and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain. It's a perfect example of how it works.
"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth.
"You create a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing. It's a perfect example of how it should not work."
Tuchel then admitted he was "a little upset" by the situation, feeling he had been tricked to "create a lot of confusion for no reason."
When asked if he had a message ahead of the game to send to Spanish fans, he added: "I sent a message but it got twisted. I said I always expect a friendly atmosphere.
"I don't expect racism, nowhere. I am shocked if it happens. It should never happen.
"I am the first person to stand up for these values. I got asked what happens if it happens and I said there are protocols in place.
"Football does what it does best, brings people together - not divides."
England midfielder Declan Rice was also questioned on the topic, where he referenced previous incidents in which the national team had experienced racism.
Montenegro were charged by UEFA in 2019 for racist behaviour after former boss Gareth Southgate confirmed racist chanting was directed at Danny Rose during a 5-1 win.
The 6-0 win against Bulgaria in Sofia in the same year was also stopped on two occasions in the first half due to racist abuse directed at players.
Speaking ahead of facing Spain, Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed. We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
"The manager hasn't brought that up yet. It wouldn't surprise me if he brings that up tomorrow. But we know where we stand.
"I'm not expecting any of that tomorrow night. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."

Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group B3 before their final game
Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says their 1-0 defeat by Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful".
Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home the winner in Linz, with the narrow victory ensuring Austria claimed top spot and automatic promotion to League A.
Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a late chance to equalise for the Republic and Hallgrimsson was frustrated they left the Raiffeisen Arena empty-handed when they had chances to secure the win which would have kept their hopes of winning the group alive.
"It was painful not to get anything from this match. I think we deserved at least a draw, but we needed the win for this game to count," he told RTE.
"I think we had the chances, the openings and the positions to do that, but this was not our day in goalscoring, so it is disappointing.
"Everything that we asked the players to do, they did and I think they gave everything.
"For that reason, we should be happy in a way but, obviously, we don't want to be building something, we want to win games."
Saturday's defeat left Hallgrimsson's side third in Group B3, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game in Dublin on Tuesday.
Hallgrimsson was left to rue Republic of Ireland's inability to clear the corner from which Kalajdzic scored.
"We actually did have a lot of chances from that second ball in the box but it kind of never fell for our players in a good position," he added.
"They have a corner that they score from on the second or third touch. That's the game at this level. You need to be switched on and focused every second of the game."
Picking up a second win in the group against Kosovo would secure second place in the group which brings with it a promotion play-off and a move up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
The Irish fell to a 1-0 defeat in Pristina in September and Hallgrimsson needs his side to finish strongly at home and pick up a vital three points.
"It was always that [Kosovo] game that was more important, but we were just so close to winning this one and being able to win the group but this is football at this level, it is all down to details."

Match report from the UEFA Nations League Group B2 match between Northern Ireland and Ukraine at Windsor Park; Terry Devlin scored his first international goal to secure a 1-0 win; Northern Ireland remain top of Group B2 with one game to play
Terry Devlin's first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.
The 23-year-old Devlin has been in the goals for Portsmouth this term with four, and opened his Northern Ireland account with a fine strike in the 68th minute as he left Ukraine goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin flat-footed with a shot from distance.
Pierce Charles then made a superb save to deny Danylo Sikan at the death and preserve Northern Ireland's fifth straight clean sheet - the first time they have achieved that since 2017 - and ensure they remain the only side in the competition yet to concede.
The three points put Northern Ireland back on top of Group B2 after Hungary's 2-0 win over Georgia earlier in the afternoon, and ruled Ukraine out of contention as they lost three straight matches for the first time in six years.
A draw in Budapest would be enough to elevate Michael O'Neill's young side to League A, while even in defeat they would face a play-off in March, and they have also earned a pot two place in next month's Euro 2028 draw.
However, O'Neill will need to watch Tuesday's match from the stands as he joined Jamie Donley - who had a first-half strike ruled out for offside - in earning a late yellow card that results in a suspension.
The match burst into life in the 23rd minute. Justin Devenny slipped the ball to Isaac Price, whose left-footed strike hit teammate Ethan Galbraith and ballooned up, falling for Donley to finish - but VAR intervened with the Luton man fractionally offside.
Moments later, Devlin's low cross found Donley at the near post but Trubin blocked his shot and then the follow-up from Shea Charles.
It was an excellent double save from the Benfica goalkeeper, who was on the bench last month when Dmytro Riznyk let in all three of Northern Ireland's shots on target in the reverse fixture.
Ukraine immediately threatened on the counter as the ball was slipped through to Olexiy Kashchuk, who outsprinted Devenny but could not beat Pierce Charles with a low strike.
Northern Ireland should have done better with an opening nine minutes into the second half.
Shea Charles, who became the youngest Northern Ireland player to reach 40 caps at the age of 23 years and nine days, laid the ball off for a well-placed Galbraith, but he hung on to it for too long before playing in Price in a crowded box, with his shot lacking the power to beat Trubin.
Trai Hume then hit a daisy-cutter which Trubin pushed around the post, and from the resulting corner Galbraith teed up Devlin's goal.
It was when Hume took a blow to the head and started bleeding that Donley's protests to referee Francois Letexier earned him a costly yellow card, and a few minutes later O'Neill followed him into the book after overreacting to a foul on Ciaron Brown.
With time ticking down, Sikan hit a firm low shot from inside the box, but Pierce Charles somehow steered it around the post to preserve the win.

Having been unbeaten in Craig Bellamy's first nine games, Wales have only won four of their past 16 matches
It can be easy to get tangled up in the complexities of Nations League permutations and, although Wales still have a few uncertainties to iron out, the picture is becoming clearer for Craig Bellamy's side.
Following their 3-1 defeat in Norway on Saturday, Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 even if they win their final game against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday.
But that does not mean they will definitely be relegated from the top tier.
Instead, they are almost certain to play one of the teams from League B in a relegation play-off in March.
However, one thing is for sure: As a result of the Norway loss, Wales will not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.
"We wanted to be in pot one. That was the drive," said head coach Bellamy after the defeat in Oslo.
"Some people might say, 'what makes you think you should be in pot one?' But I do.
"Maybe I'm naïve. I see in big parts of that game we can be in pot one. Let's take the good bits from the game, definitely improve on certain moments of the game and just keep pushing."
A point against Portugal would make sure of it, but even if they lose, Wales will most likely end up in a relegation play-off.
Only the two worst-performing sides will be automatically relegated to League B.
With one game left, the other bottom teams in League A - Turkey, the Czech Republic and Serbia - all have no points, whereas Wales have three.
For them to finish among the worst two, they would need to lose to Portugal, and two of the other teams would need to win their final fixture with a significant swing in goal difference.
Wales have a goal difference of -5. Considering Turkey (-10) visit France, Czech Republic (-10) are in Croatia and Serbia (-7) travel to Greece, it would require an unlikely turn of events for Bellamy's men to be automatically relegated.
Wales have conceded eight goals during this Nations League campaign
The relegation play-offs will be held across two legs at the end of March, with the first leg between March 25-27, and the second between March 28-30.
As a League A side, Wales will be seeded and therefore play at home in the second leg.
The draw for the play-offs takes place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland, on Friday, 20 November.
The sides that finish in the top two of League A's four groups will also discover the quarter-final draw on the same day.
Slovenia, Northern Ireland, Kosovo and Bosnia-Herzegovina are currently all in second place in their groups.
However, Scotland, Ukraine, Austria, the Republic of Ireland and Poland could also be potential opponents.
Wales have scored three goals in five games during this Nations League campaign
All teams finishing third or higher in League A will be named as top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.
By missing out, Wales could now be drawn alongside one of Europe's heavyweights in their group.
Spain, France, Italy, Netherlands and Portugal are among the sides already guaranteed pot one seeding for the draw on 6 December in Belfast.
England will also be a top seed, although Thomas Tuchel's men will be kept apart from Wales and the other Euro 2028 co-hosts in qualifying regardless.
When it comes to reaching the Euros, the 12 group winners and eight best-ranked runners-up qualify directly.
For any of the co-hosts who don't make it via that route, there are two automatic spots available. Those will be awarded to the best-ranked between the four nations who haven't qualified directly.
If Wales still haven't made it, there is still the back-up option of the play-offs.
And given play-off places are based on Nations League rankings, Wales are highly likely to already have that safety net.

Üstelik ortada somut bir eleştiri olmasa bile insanların seni nasıl değerlendirdiğine dair tahminler yürütüyor olabilirsin. Bu durum, kendini sürekli geliştirmeye çalışan ve sorumluluklarını önemseyen biri olmanla ilişkili olabilir. Ancak gelişmek için kendini sürekli suçlaman gerekmez. Hatta kendine yönelttiğin yoğun eleştiriler zaman zaman harekete geçmeni zorlaştırabilir. Bir işe başlamadan önce yeterince iyi yapamayacağını düşünmek, karar verirken defalarca fikir değiştirmek veya başarı elde ettiğinde bile rahatlayamamak bu döngünün parçaları olabilir. Kendine koyduğun standartlar o kadar yüksek olabilir ki hiçbir başarı sana yeterli gelmeyebilir. Burada üzerinde durman gereken şey, kendini eleştirmeyi tamamen bırakmak değil, eleştirinin dozunu ve dilini değiştirmek. Bir hata yaptığında kendine neden böyle yaptığını sorabilirsin ama kendini aşağılamak zorunda değilsin. Bir başkasının seni sevmesi için kusursuz olman gerekmediği gibi, kendine değer vermek için de her zaman başarılı olman gerekmiyor. Kendini yalnızca yaptıkların üzerinden değerlendirmemeyi öğrenmek, bu zihinsel yükü hafifletmenin önemli adımlarından biri olabilir.
Kendine yönelttiğin eleştiriler hayatının pek çok alanına yayılmış olabilir. Söylediğin bir cümleden aldığın bir karara, tamamladığın bir işten sosyal ilişkilerine kadar birçok konuda kendini sorguluyor olabilirsin. Üstelik çoğu zaman başkalarının sana yöneltmediği eleştirileri kendi içinde üretiyor olman mümkün. Birinin yüz ifadesini yanlış yorumlayabilir, kısa bir mesajı defalarca okuyabilir veya geçmişte yaşadığın bir olayı zihninde tekrar tekrar canlandırabilirsin. Sanki sürekli kendini değerlendiren görünmez bir jüri varmış gibi hissedebilirsin. Bu yoğun öz eleştiri, kendinden çok şey beklediğini ve hata yapmaya karşı tahammülünün düşük olabileceğini düşündürüyor. Başarılı olduğunda bile rahatlayamamak, başkalarının onayına ihtiyaç duymak, dinlenirken suçluluk hissetmek veya kendini başkalarıyla kıyaslamak seni zihinsel açıdan yorabilir. Zamanla kendi ihtiyaçlarını ikinci plana atabilir ve çevrendeki insanların beklentilerini karşılamaya çalışırken ne istediğini unutabilirsin. En zorlayıcı tarafı ise kendine ne kadar çabalarsan çabala yeterli olmadığını hissettirebilmesidir. Öncelikle kendinle kurduğun ilişkinin değişebileceğini bilmelisin. Her düşüncenin doğru olmadığını, her hatanın telafi edilebileceğini ve herkesin zaman zaman yanlış kararlar verebildiğini hatırlamak önemli. Kendini yargıladığın anlarda, aynı durumda sevdiğin birine ne söyleyeceğini düşünmek sana farklı bir bakış açısı kazandırabilir. Bu düşünceler yoğunlaşıyor, günlük yaşamını, ilişkilerini veya ruh hâlini belirgin biçimde etkiliyorsa bir ruh sağlığı uzmanından destek almak da faydalı olabilir. Unutma, kendine karşı nazik olmak bir zayıflık değil; kendinle kurduğun ilişkinin temel ihtiyaçlarından biri.

Pragmatic, resolute and gutsy. Sonia Bompastor showed her ruthless side and delivered a tactical masterclass as Chelsea earned a 1-0 win over Manchester City and leapfrogged them at the top of the Women’s Super League.
Lucy Bronze credited fellow full-back Katie McCabe with firing Chelsea up pre-match, having told them they “had to be dogs” in the game, and a dogged performance followed. Sandy Baltimore’s stunning strike in added time at the end of the first half was the difference as the west London side nullified the threat of a team that had scored in each of their preceding 21 games in all competitions, inflicting their first loss of the campaign.
The task for City got even tougher when goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita received a straight red for clattering into Alyssa Thompson, but despite their numerical disadvantage it was end to end right up until the final whistle.
“It always affects you when you go one player down,” said manager Andrée Jeglertz. “But we handled that and that’s not why we lose the game. I think it’s small details. It’s a tight game, it’s two great football teams, there’s a lot of situations, there’s a lot of battles and they managed to score on their big chance from a great finish. We also have a couple of great opportunities where we don’t manage to score.”
Momentum was with City going into the match after their 5-0 defeat of West Ham the preceding weekend and a 4-1 win against Inter in the Champions League on Tuesday night and they were able to welcome the injured duo Vivianne Miedema and Beth Mead back to the bench to bolster their matchday squad.
At Stamford Bridge the England women’s manager, Sarina Wiegman, the US women’s manager, Emma Hayes, and passionate women’s football advocate and pundit Ian Wright were in the stands. It was a fixture that promised much, and it delivered: the league’s most potent attacks, with Chelsea having scored 28 league goals before this fixture to City’s 27, while Bompastor’s side had the most solid defence, having conceded only five times before kick-off.
Manchester United captain Maya le Tissier marked her 150th appearance for the club with a superb strike in a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace at the Progress with Unity Stadium. Presented with a framed shirt before kick-off, Le Tissier whipped a low shot from distance into the net in the 18th minute before Elisabeth Terland confirmed United’s win after the hour mark.
United moved up to fourth with the win and they kept hold of the position after Tottenham drew a blank in a goalless draw at home to Everton , whose winless run in the league stretched to five matches. In the day’s late game, Liverpool ended a five-match winless run in the WSL by easing past Brighton 3-0. Press Association
It was a chess match. After a thrillingly frenetic start there was a change for Chelsea just 12 minutes in, with the centre-back Kadeisha Buchanan replaced by Veerle Buurman. There was speculation over whether the withdrawal of the Canadian defender was due to injury and Bompastor unconvincingly claimed it was.
“Yesterday in training, she got a knock to her head during contact with a teammate. She was fine after the training session. She was fine in the evening. We assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,” she said. “I just felt watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. Then I took the responsibility to make the substitution. But for me, I was almost forced to do that because I know my player and I know she was not in the game.”
However, if, as many believe, the defensive switch was a tactical decision, it was a stroke of genius, as Buurman was excellent at nullifying the threat of Khadija Shaw.
“She had a really good performance against a top player,” said Bompastor. “Today was positive. But again, as I’ve told you previously, when it doesn’t work it’s not so positive.”
There were chances at both ends but they were limited and it took until the fourth of five added minutes for Chelsea to draw first blood. The goal was sensational. Baltimore collected the ball just inside the box on the right, from Ellie Carpenter, lined up her shot and sent a piledriver of a strike into the roof of the net.
City sought an instant reply after the break but they could not find a way through and momentum ebbed and flowed. Jeglertz withdrew Sam Coffey and Mary Fowler in favour of Miedema and Laura Blindkilde Brown to help his side assert some authority in the middle and, through Miedema, to add some creative instinct.
However, as City pushed they left themselves vulnerable on the break and when Maika Hamano’s crossfield ball was met by Alyssa Thompson with just over 15 minutes remaining it was disaster for City. Yamashita raced out of her box and clattered into the Chelsea forward, conceding a free-kick and receiving a straight red card.
Despite City’s efforts, Chelsea were in control and they held strong to blow the title race wide open.

In any big encounter you will often hear managers say it is the "fine margins" that decide a game of football.
Sometimes it is luck. Sometimes it is individual brilliance. But on Saturday it was Sonia Bompastor's bold decisions that helped Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0.
The top-of-the-table Women's Super League clash was as intriguing as you would hope it to be and both managers needed to be on their toes.
Chelsea boss Bompastor "took responsibility" and brought off struggling defender Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes in, and it had the desired effect.
City striker Khadija Shaw was not able to get in behind like she had done in the early stages, and Buchanan's replacement Veerle Buurman shone.
When the fourth official's board went up showing the number of the player Buurman would replace, there was confusion from Chelsea players.
It was clearly not planned, nor had Buchanan asked to come off. There was no apparent injury as she jogged off and she was clearly upset, heading straight down the tunnel.
Asked to clarify the situation, Bompastor said: "Yesterday in training she got a knock to her head in contact with a team-mate but she was fine.
"She was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine. I had that information before the game.
"But I felt from watching her at the beginning of the game that she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make the substitution.
"I felt I was almost forced to do that. I know my player and she was not in the game."
Whether Buchanan's shaky start was down to that knock is unclear, but Bompastor knew her decision was a risk and was willing to act immediately.
Buurman instantly marshalled Shaw, and City's early threat was quietened as Chelsea regained control and ended the half a goal up thanks to Sandy Baltimore.
Shaw did not record a shot on target and in-form England international Lauren Hemp was quiet as Buurman performed well in a stubborn Chelsea backline.
City manager Andree Jeglertz said he did not think the switch "changed the picture", but he was outsmarted by Bompastor during the 90 minutes.
Bompastor admitted she had not spoken properly with Buchanan at full-time but promised to "explain myself to her".
"I just told her a few words. My assistant coach Camille Abily will have done that already probably and I think everything will be fine," said the Frenchwoman.
"I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I'm always direct and honest so they have the information. It won't be any different."
The risky substitution was compounded by an injury to striker Melvine Malard 23 minutes later, meaning Chelsea's XI was tweaked twice before half-time.
Not normally one to bring on players at the break, Bompastor was smart and hooked goalscorer Baltimore, who was likely still buzzing from her impact.
She was replaced by Maika Hamano, who went on to play the ball through to Alyssa Thompson when she was brought down by City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita, and she was shown a straight red card as a result, ending the visitors' comeback hopes.
"We knew going into the second half we only had one substitution slot and we knew Sandy has been playing lots of minutes," said Bompastor.
"I knew she probably didn't have the legs to go more than maybe 60 minutes and I knew I didn't have more slots after that. I was forced into this one as well.
"It paid off and that's good. Sandy was doing well but she knows the reason why we made that decision.
"That's the first time I experienced that kind of substitution in the first half. It's good for my own experience."
Bompastor's bravery was rewarded and, while City certainly had their chances, Chelsea defended resiliently to see out the narrow win.
Jeglertz could not find a solution to Chelsea's attacking threats, which came largely from wide areas via Ellie Carpenter and Thompson.
Vivianne Miedema returned from injury and looked sharp when she came on for City in the second half, but it was not enough to change the result.
In contrast, Bompastor's risks proved the difference, and they were made with former Chelsea boss Emma Hayes, who mastered the art of bullish decisions, watching on in the stands alongside Sarina Wiegman at Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea's victory bumped them back up to the WSL summit, a point above City, while Buurman picked up the player-of-the-match award.
"It paid off today. You have to be brave to make that decision in that moment because you know bringing in a player in the game is a risk," said Bompastor.
"We had a good conversation with Veerle and she was clear on why she wasn't starting the game. That clarity was important for when she came in.
"She had a really good performance against a top player. Sometimes when it doesn't work, it's not so positive, but today it was.
"You have to react and be the one that analyses the situation and make decisions. I'm used to it, even if you don't see lots of substitutions in the first half most of the time in football."

Match report from the UEFA Nations League Group A4 match between Norway and Wales at Ullevaal Stadion; Norway won 3-1 thanks to goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland; Wales now bottom of Group A4 as threat of relegation grows
Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo despite a spirited performance, as the threat of relegation to the second tier of the Nations League now looms over Craig Bellamy's side.
Wales looked the better side in the first half and had chances to take the lead, most notably through Daniel James on three occasions, before they unravelled after half-time.
Antonio Nusa showed why he is often referred to as the Norwegian Neymar as he broke the deadlock with his fine strike into the bottom left corner before substitute Andreas Schjelderup tapped home Erling Haaland's pass to give the hosts a commanding lead.
David Brooks' sublime chipped finish sparked hopes of a comeback but Haaland's penalty, after Connor Roberts pushed Schjelderup down in the box, punctured the late momentum they had gathered.
Wales are now guaranteed to finish bottom of Group A4 with a worse head-to-head record against Denmark and Norway - the two teams they could have potentially drawn level with on six points by beating Portugal in their final group game in Cardiff.
A draw against Portugal on Tuesday would guarantee Wales a Nations League relegation play-off in March against a League B runner-up.
Wales knew finishing in the top three of their Nations League group would see them join Europe's heavyweights in pot one at next month's Euros draw in Belfast.
"We wanted to be in pot one. That was the drive," Wales boss Bellamy said of missing out on top seed status in Euro 2028 qualifying.
"Some people might say, 'What makes you think you should be in pot one?'. But I do.
"Maybe I'm naive. I see in big parts of that game today that we can be in pot one.
"Let's take the good bits from the game, definitely improve on certain moments of the game and just keep pushing."
Wales will be Euro 2028 co-hosts alongside England, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland - and actually get the tournament under way in Cardiff should they qualify.
"There is loads for us to improve on but I've liked a lot of it, I have to be honest.
"It's not that we want to sit in, we always look at the pressure on the ball and I thought at times first half we did that really well.
"When we tried to trigger, we were able to move the ball well, and then turn into attack for us even from deep areas.
"So it was a lot of good things, but in the second half I just felt we lost a bit of momentum. We lost a bit of energy and that was a difficult period."
Wales were energised by their substitutions as Bournemouth forward Brooks and Cardiff playmaker Rubin Colwill brought new life to the attack.
Bellamy said: "I thought Rubin and Broosky were top and 'Sparky' (Mark Harris) brought the energy and the intensity he's going to give you.
"I thought the subs really gave us that push again and we got it to 2-1.
"But we made a mistake and it falls to a player who was offside, but then he isn't offside by the time he hits the ball."
"A reminder Wales have Portugal in their final group game on Tuesday.
"Even a win won't be enough to get off bottom spot due to head-to-head records with Denmark and Norway.
"They will avoid automatic relegation to tier B, though, if they don't finish as one of the two worst bottom-placed sides in tier A.
"Wales are on three points, with the other bottom sides in tier A currently on 0 points.
"A relegation play-off against a side from tier B would be the alternative."

Terry Devlin scored his first Northern Ireland goal against Ukraine
When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind.
And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far.
Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast.
They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner.
It leaves Northern Ireland's Nations League fate in their own hands, and a draw or better in Hungary would secure promotion to League A for the first time.
For Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill, it was a huge moment from a player who he said is "a bit of a dream" to manage.
"Terry's a great lad. He deserves everything he'll get from the game and he's one of those lads that maximises what he has," O'Neill said about the 23-year-old Portsmouth defender.
Northern Ireland beat Ukraine to move closer to Nations League promotion
Speaking about his versatility - Devlin can play in midfield as well as a full-back on either side - O'Neill added: "He does it with no fuss. He tries to do it to the best of his ability.
"He's a bit of a dream for a manager and he has the ability to contribute goals."
The average age of O'Neill's starting XI on Saturday was just 22.9 with eight players aged 23 or younger.
Devlin epitomises what this team are all about with his all-action display rewarded with a first international goal.
A versatile option, he broke through into senior football with his hometown club Dungannon Swifts in the Irish Premiership and impressive performances for Glentoran saw him earn a move to Portsmouth in 2023.
He has now become a cult hero at Fratton Park, and he is the club's top scorer in the Championship this season.
His winner in Belfast was a fitting moment for a player who continues to grow on the international stage.
"He's a very valuable player for Portsmouth and I think he's in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that."
While Devlin will get the headlines after his man-of-the-match performance, goalkeeper Pierce Charles came up with a big moment of his own with a superb reflex save to deny Danylo Sikan in the closing stages.
The 21-year-old has yet to concede in the Nations League campaign, and he has produced several big moments to make it 466 minutes and counting without shipping a goal for Northern Ireland.
"You don't keep five clean sheets because you're good with the ball at your feet. You keep five clean sheets because you make good decisions," said O'Neill.
"You make saves when it's needed. He kind of does it without any fuss as well, which I think is really good.
"He doesn't come and cause any issues with the back-three, which is very important for any goalkeeper, and he has a good decision-making process and a good understanding of the game."
Northern Ireland will now head to Hungary with their Nations League destiny in their own hands in what is essentially a Group B2 decider.
They are guaranteed a promotion play-off at the very least, but the goal will be to earn automatic elevation to League A for the first time.
Highlights: Devlin nets first international goal to seal victory
Considering Northern Ireland had just one Nations League win in 16 League B matches before the campaign, back-to-back promotions would be a remarkable achievement.
One down side from the win over Ukraine was the two yellow cards accumulated, one for O'Neill and the other for key striker Jamie Donley.
Both were for reactions to a perceived lack of decisions from French referee Francois Letexier, and both manager and player will now watch the game in Budapest from the stands.
"The referee doesn't like my reaction and there's not much I can do about that," O'Neill said.
"I would assume that I'm going to have to watch the game from the stands, but I'll be able to influence it from there, I'm sure."
On Donley's booking, which came for protesting after Letexier failed to stop play when Trai Hume was bleeding from a cut on his head, O'Neill said it was a "poor yellow".
"I thought Jamie had a very good game for us. He'll be a blow for us," he said.
Terry Devlin started his professional career in the Irish Premiership
But the suspensions will do little to dampen what was another encouraging night at Windsor Park.
Hungary had piled the pressure on Northern Ireland by winning in Georgia earlier on Saturday, and Northern Ireland's response sets up a showdown to top the group on Tuesday.
"We were aware that Hungary had won the game earlier and we're in a great position," O'Neill added.
"It would be great to win the group. It will be a tough, tough game but this is a brilliant game for us. It's a great arena to play in."
Having kept five clean sheets in as many matches, O'Neill is targeting completing the campaign without conceding.
If they can do that, they would not only win promotion but secure a play-off for Euro 2028 as a back-up should their qualifying group not go to plan.
"For a nation of our size, with our players at this stage of their careers, to have a chance to win the group and also to be playing Nations League A is a big achievement.
"I think we would probably be one of the smaller nations to play at Nations League A level since the start of the competition.
"We want to try to achieve that and we have a chance to do that on Tuesday night."

A Milli Takım'ın unutulmaz kalecisi Rüştü Reçber, Radyospor'a ay-yıldızlı ekip hakkında açıklamalarda bulundu.
Reçber, genç yıldızın golünü överken Sergen Yalçın'ın 1996 yılında kendisine Kadıköy'de attığı golle de kıyasladı.
Sergen Yalçın ve ekibine başarılar dileyen Reçber, şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Sergen Yalçın ve ekibine başarılar diliyorum. Umarım başarılı olur. Milli Takıma geldiğimizde mental olarak iyi durumda değiliz. Hala Dünya Kupası ’nın etkisindeyiz. Kötü bir Dünya Kupası geçirdik. Sonrasında Uluslar Ligi’nde peş peşe 5 maç kaybettik. Bunun etkisi takımın üzerinde. Bir an önce Dünya Kupası ve Uluslar Ligi’nin hayal kırıklığından uzaklaşmamız lazım. Bunu Sergen Hoca ve ekibi düzeltecektir."
Arda Güler'in Belçika karşısında attığı golü de değerlendiren Rüştü Reçber , genç futbolcuya övgüler yağdırdı.
Reçber, Arda'nın golünü Sergen Yalçın 'ın 1996 yılında kendisine Kadıköy'de attığı golle kıyaslayarak şu sözleri söyledi:
" Arda Güler ’in Belçika’ya attığı golü her futbolcu atamaz. Vurmadan sol ayağıyla topu göndereceği yeri hesapladı. Bence Arda’nın Belçika’ya attığı gol, Sergen’in 1996’da Kadıköy’de bana attığı golden daha güzeldi."

Milli basketbolcu Alperen Şengün, NBA Kupası'nda Utah Jazz karşısında 43 sayı, 12 ribaunt ve 5 asistlik bir performansa imza attı. Bu istatistikle Houston Rockets tarihinde 40 sayı, 10 ribaunt ve 5 asist barını aşan üçüncü oyuncu oldu. Önünde yalnızca Yao Ming ile James Harden bulunuyor.
Toyota Center'da oynanan karşılaşmada hücumda takımını sırtlayan Şengün, performansıyla kulüp tarihine de adını yazdırdı. Rockets formasıyla bu üçlü barajı daha önce yalnızca Yao Ming ve James Harden aşabilmişti. Milli oyuncu, 12 ribaunt ve 5 asistle 'double-double' tamamladı.
Houston, Şengün'ün 43 sayısıyla Utah Jazz'ı 125-118 mağlup etti. Rockets'ta Kevin Durant 22 sayı attı, Tari Eason 14 sayı ve 11 ribaunt, Amen Thompson ise 12 sayı ve 10 ribaunt üretti. Jazz'da Darryn Peterson 28, Keyonte George 27, Ace Bailey 21 sayıyla oynadı.
NBA Kupası'nın bir başka maçında Los Angeles Clippers, konuk ettiği Oklahoma City Thunder'ı tek sayı farkla geçti. Yalı Çapkını dizisiyle geniş kitlelere ulaşan Mert Ramazan Demir'in yeni projesi belli oldu.
Necati Cumalı 'nın eserinden uyarlanan ve 1963 yılında Metin Erksan'ın yönetmenliğinde beyazperdeye taşınan " Susuz Yaz", bu kez dizi oluyor. Demir, yapımda Osman karakterine hayat verecek.
Yeni rolü hakkında konuşan Mert Ramazan Demir, " Susuz Yaz"ın Türk sinemasındaki önemine değinerek projede yer almaktan duyduğu heyecanı paylaştı.
Demir, "Metin Erksan imzalı 'Susuz Yaz', Türk sinema tarihinde çok güzel yer etmiş bir film. Necati Cumalı'nın 'Susuz Yaz' kitabındaki bir öyküsünden, 70 sayfalık bir alıntı. Çok güzel bir ekiple çalışıyoruz, bu ekibin bir parçası olmaktan çok mutluyum" ifadelerini kullandı.
1970'li yılların Adana'sında geçecek dizide, Çarlak köyünde yaşayan iki kardeşin hayatını değiştiren gelişmeler konu alınacak. Senaryosunu Sema Ergenekon'un yazdığı dizinin yönetmenliğini Yusuf Pirhasan ve Mehmet Can Bindal üstleniyor.
Mert Ramazan Demir'in başrolünde yer aldığı dizide Lizge Cömert, Batuhan Bozkurt Yüzgüleç, Şebnem Bozoklu, İrem Sak, Serpil Gül, Deniz Celiloğlu ve Umut Kurt rol alacak.
Oyuncu kadrosunda ayrıca Şirin Sultan Saldamlı, Güneş Sayın, Begüm Akkaya, Ilgım İpekçi, Meriç Rakalar, Özgür Daniel Foster, Kayra Zabcı, Esra Ünnü ve Kemal Burak Alper de bulunuyor.
Ay Yapım tarafından hazırlanan "Susuz Yaz"ın yayın tarihi henüz açıklanmadı.
